body.p: Claims 1-17 and 20 are pending in the present application. Claim 1 is amended in this paper. No claims are canceled in this paper. No new claims are added in this paper.
In taking the foregoing actions, Applicant respectfully submits Applicant is not

necessarily conceding in this application that these claims, as originally presented, are not patentable over the references cited by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), as pertinent ones of the present claim amendments and cancellations are only for facilitating expeditious prosecution. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the canceled claims and/or other claims in one or more continuing applications.
An Applicant-initiated interview was conducted on December 28, 2023, between

Examiner Curry and Applicant's representative, Shixiong Wang, Reg. No. 79,880. Objections tothe drawings as well as rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 112 and 103 were discussed. Applicant thanks the Examiner for her time and consideration. An agreement was reached that the replacement sheet and the proposed claim amendment submitted overcome the objections to the drawings and the § 112 rejections. An agreement was also reached that claim 1 as amended overcomes the references of record cited in the instant Office Action, pending a further search.
The drawings are objected to as "the chamber must be shown or the feature(s) canceled from the claim(s)." Office Action, p. 2.
In response, a replacement sheet for Fig. 2 is submitted with this paper to show chamber 142.

As agreed to in the above-noted interview, the replacement sheet of Fig. 2 is sufficient to overcome the objections to the drawings. As such, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of the objections to the drawings.
Claims 1-17 and 20 were rejected pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor
regards as the invention. Specifically, the Examiner states "[c]laim 1, lines 3 and 4, recite limitation 'chamber'. It is unclear what element this is referring to." Office Action, p. 3.
Without conceding to the propriety of the rejection, and solely in the interest of

advancing prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to recite "wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel."

As agreed to in the above-noted interview, claim 1 as amended overcomes the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that this rejection is now moot, and respectfully requests that the rejections of claims 1-17 and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) be withdrawn.
Epstein/Clark/Struzik/Glaser/Paget
Claims 1, 6-11, 13-17 and 20 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly

unpatentable over U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20150344143 Al to Epstein; Michael Jay et al. (hereinafter "Epstein"), in view of U. S. Patent No. 6422514 Bl to Clark; William James et al. (hereinafter "Clark") in view of U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20130197791 Al to Struzik; Anthony (hereinafter "Struzik"), and further in view of U.S. Patent Appl. Publ. No. 20110042520 Al to Glaser; Daniel et al. (hereinafter "Glaser"), and further in view of U.S. Patent. Office Action, p. 4. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection. Claim 1
Claim las amended recites:
A method for fueling and using an aircraft, wherein the method comprises:
conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner
wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into
the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel;
storing, using the fuel tank comprising the chamber between the inner wall and the outer
wall of the fuel tank, wherein the chamber is configured to insulate the liquid gas fuel by prevention of condensation of humidity within the fuel tank of the aircraft;
fueling, using a fuel line, the aircraft, wherein fueling further comprises:

filling the fuel tank with liquified gas fuel to a desired level, wherein the desired level comprises fuel for a plurality of flights plus reserves, wherein a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related insulation of the fuel tank, wherein the sensor is configured to: detect humidity within the fuel tank; and
convert the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and
removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft; and
preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level; and
flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas fuel.

The Office has not asserted that Epstein discloses "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel" as amended in claim 1. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Epstein does not disclose "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." As agreed to in the above-noted interview, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Clark does not cure the deficiency of Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Clark teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Clark does not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Clark, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Struzik does not cure the deficiency of Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Struzik teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Struzik does not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas

fuel." Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, and Struzki, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Glaser does not cure the deficiency of Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Glaser teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Glaser does not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Therefore, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzki, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Paget does not cure the deficiency of Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Paget teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Paget does not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." As such, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzki, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at
least the reasons discussed above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of this rejection.

Each of claims 6-11, 13-17 and 20 depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 6-11, 13-17 and 20 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, Glaser, and Paget, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed
above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of these rejections.
Epstein/Clark/Struzik/Glaser/D'Auvergne

Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable Epstein, Clark, Struzik and Glaser as applied to claims above, and further in view of US 7281682 B2 D'Auvergne; Hector A. (hereinafter "D'Auvergne"). Office Action, p. 7. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Claim 2 depends directly from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 2 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of this rejection.
Epstein/Glaser/Wexler/Connor
Claims 3-5

Claims 3-5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable over Epstein and Glaser as applied to claims above, in view of US 6123295 Al Wexler; Mark Harry et al. (hereinafter "Wexler") and further in view of NPL "What is Aerogel" by Nick Connor (hereinafter "Conner"). Office Action, p. 8. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Each of claims 3-5 depends from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3-5 are patentably distinguishable over Epstein and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Wexler and Connor fail to cure the deficiencies of Epstein and Glaser. The Office has not asserted that Wexler nor Conor teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that Wexler and Connor do not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." As such, Applicant respectfully submits that claims 3-5 as amended are patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Wexler, and Connor, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of this rejection.
Epstein/Clark/Struzik/Glaser/Benassi

Claim 12 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly unpatentable Epstein, Clark, Struzik and Glaser as applied to claims above, and further in view of US 20120119032 Al Benassi; Eric et al. Office Action, p. 9. Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection.

Claim 12 depends, directly or indirectly, from claim 1. As noted above, claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 12 is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzik, and Glaser, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above.

Benassi does not cure the deficiency of Epstein. The Office has not asserted that Benassi teaches, suggests, or motivates "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." Accordingly, Applicant

respectfully submits that Benassi does not teach, suggest, or motivate "conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, and wherein clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel." As such, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 1 as amended is patentably distinguishable over Epstein, Clark, Struzki, Glaser, and Benassi, alone or in combination, for at least the reasons discussed above. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of this rejection.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully submits that all claims in the application are in a

condition for allowance and respectfully solicit the prompt issuance of a Notice of Allowance. If any issues remain, the Examiner is encouraged to call the undersigned practitioner at the number listed below.
Respectfully submitted,
